head_policy.description: For an active branch task, the live task/PR head may differ from task_head only by descendant commits whose complete diff from task_head is restricted to the canonical execution-state file. Completed merged tasks retain their accepted code task_head plus explicit merge evidence.

acceptance_criteria: resources/js/pages/Systems.jsx must not import or consume resources/js/data/catalog.js or platform/store.jsx/useStore as live-route business authority.

Systems.jsx live customer routes must not branch on apiBackend to legacy implementations; Laravel/API contracts must be the sole business-authority path while preserving existing route URLs and customer-facing visual behavior.

Orders, checkout and other Systems.jsx domains must use server-issued state for inventory, pricing, payments, shipping, wallet conversion, order status and related business values; client fallback constants such as a hardcoded coins-per-rupee authority must not substitute missing server truth.
API failure must fail closed with an explicit unavailable/error state and must never fall back to static catalog, localStorage orders or other legacy business data.
P1-C must stay consumer-scoped: do not delete the global StoreProvider, platform/store.jsx or resources/js/data/catalog.js until remaining consumers are migrated and P1-D proves them unused.
The frontend fast gate must reject future Systems.jsx reintroduction of apiBackend legacy routing, useStore business authority or static catalog imports.
Targeted browser coverage, frontend quality checks, production build and applicable repository CI/governance acceptance must pass on the exact PR head before merge.

architecture_decisions.decision: Treat canonical-state-only descendant commits as code-equivalent to task_head for head reconciliation and hosted acceptance evidence.
architecture_decisions.reason: A commit cannot embed its own final SHA inside the state file it contains; without this rule every canonical-state update would invalidate itself.

architecture_decisions.decision: VSN Commerce original project materials are proprietary / closed-source; project metadata must not grant GPLv3 or another open-source project license without a new explicit owner decision.
architecture_decisions.reason: Repository owner explicitly rejected GPLv3 on 2026-08-28; ADR-0001 records the decision while preserving third-party licenses.

architecture_decisions.decision: Remove residual client-side/static authority in small domain batches before retiring the global StoreProvider or redesigning Admin.
architecture_decisions.reason: Current Laravel mode is mandatory, but residual unreachable legacy branches still create dual-authority regression risk; consumer-first removal is safer than a giant deletion.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use Product.jsx as the second P1 consumer-first batch before Systems.jsx and global StoreProvider retirement.
architecture_decisions.reason: Product.jsx directly imported the static catalog and global store and contained multiple apiBackend branches; P1-B removed that consumer-side legacy authority while preserving Laravel contracts.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use Systems.jsx as the third P1 consumer-first batch and migrate its customer-system domains incrementally before global StoreProvider retirement.
architecture_decisions.reason: Systems.jsx still directly imports apiBackend, useStore and the static catalog and contains Laravel-vs-Legacy route forks for live customer workflows. Removing those consumer-side branches before P1-D is the smallest safe path to proving the legacy engine unused.

known_risks: AGENTS.md still contains stale P0-01, P0-02 and P0-03 status text from the 2026-08-22 audit; repository evidence and this canonical checkpoint supersede those historical status labels until the plan document is reconciled.

Systems.jsx still contains extensive Laravel-vs-Legacy route branching and imports apiBackend, useStore and the static catalog; P1-C is active to remove those live-route authority forks without redesigning the storefront.

The global StoreProvider is still mounted in resources/js/main.jsx and platform/store.jsx retains localStorage-backed business authority; it must not be removed until its consumers are migrated and P1-D proves the legacy engine unused.
Third-party dependencies retain their own license obligations even though the project-level VSN Commerce materials are proprietary.
